definitions.explanation: A small, cylindrical charcoal cooking brazier traditionally made of diatomaceous earth ({珪藻土|けいそうど}). Used in homes and restaurants for grilling fish, meat, and vegetables one piece at a time.

examples.japanese: {七輪|しちりん}で{秋刀魚|さんま}を{焼|や}いた。
examples.english: I grilled saury on a shichirin.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}では{七輪|しちりん}で{肉|にく}を{焼|や}いて{食|た}べる。
examples.english: At this restaurant you grill the meat yourself on a shichirin.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}に{七輪|しちりん}を{出|だ}して、{家族|かぞく}で{魚|さかな}や{野菜|やさい}を{焼|や}いて{楽|たの}しんだ。
examples.english: We brought the shichirin out into the garden and had fun grilling fish and vegetables as a family.

notes:
Said to come from the older practice of selling enough charcoal for one use at the price of {七厘|しちりん} (seven rin, a tiny denomination). The diatomaceous-earth body insulates the heat well, allowing strong grilling with little fuel.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {七輪|しちりん}で{焼|や}く: to grill on a shichirin
- {七輪|しちりん}{焼|や}き: shichirin-grilled (dish style)
- {炭|すみ}を{七輪|しちりん}に{入|い}れる: to put charcoal in the shichirin

CULTURAL NOTE:
Long associated with home cooking of grilled fish ({秋刀魚|さんま}, {鯵|あじ}) and now also popular in {焼|やき}{鳥|とり} and {焼|やき}{肉|にく} restaurants that serve a personal grill per table.
